text:
sylvia: Starting an experiment for an "adaptive holdback" strategy to improve scale-to-zero economics. TL;DR: keep a tiny predictive buffer of GPUs that adapts per region/workload instead of a fixed warm pool. Want to run for 2 weeks and measure p99 coldstart, cost delta, and incident count.

jay: sounds promising. how will we predict demand? ML model or heuristics? :thinking:

sylvia: heuristics first. windowed request rate + short-term trend. if rate increases > 20% in 30s we immediately raise holdback. fallback to model later.

leo: curious about interactions with cluster-autoscaler and node draining. CA sometimes under-reacts if pods have long init. Are we planning any readiness gating to avoid jitter?

anita: we should use a PodReadinessGate + custom prewarm sidecar for model servers so they mark ready only after KV cache is warmed. avoids user-visible cold tails.

jay: can you paste the config we plan to use? would like to review limits and cooldowns.

sylvia: sure, here's the alpha config we'll roll to staging (very small footgun):

```yaml
holdback:
  min_gpus: 0
  max_extra_percent: 15  # cap extra nodes as pct of current pool
  scale_up_window: 30s
  scale_down_cooldown: 10m
  prediction_window: 60s
  region_overrides:
    eu-west-1:
      max_extra_percent: 10
    us-west-2:
      max_extra_percent: 20
```

leo: scale_down_cooldown 10m feels long but safer for p99. What's the cost math on that versus fixed warm pool?

anita: quick calc from last 30 days traffic baseline: keeping a 5% fixed warm pool in us-west-2 => ~$12k/month. With adaptive holdback and 10m cooldown we estimate ~$4k-6k/month depending on burstiness. Need real A/B to confirm.

jay: what about preemptible/spot nodes? we saw a spike when 2 spots reclaimed simultaneously and autoscaler couldn't replace GPUs fast enough. How do we handle multi-AZ fallbacks?

sylvia: plan: prefer non-preemptible for holdback nodes; if we do spot, double the holdback size and place across AZs. Also add policy to immediately fallback to smaller CPU model variant in extreme shortage.

infra-bot: deployment created: refs/heads/feature/adaptive-holdback -> staging cluster. CI: 9182c4a.

leo: one failure mode to watch: node-pool shrink racing with holdback scale-up. If CA drains nodes while the holdback controller is trying to allocate new nodes we might get thundering coldstarts. Recommend adding a nodepool annotation to pause autoscaler for 45s while holdback scale-up is in progress.

anita: agree. also add metric emissions: holdback_size, holdback_desired, holdback_actual, coldstart_duration_ms, cost_delta_usd_hour. We'll wire into console dashboards and set an alert if p99 > 1.2s.

jay: for the A/B, which routes are in cohort A vs B?

sylvia: A = interactive chat endpoints (low latency SLA), B = batch/rerank endpoints. We'll start with 20% traffic on A -> adaptive, 80% control. If p99 regression < 5% and cost drops > 30% we scale up rollout.

leo: operational checklist for oncall: rollback hook, manual holdback override, and a quick script to convert holdback nodes to drainable nodes in an emergency. Add runbook note.

anita: I'll draft runbook. one more thought: add a short fast-backoff path for sudden epidemic traffic where we temporarily disable scale-to-zero for that workload for 30m.

jay: ack. when do we flip this into staging?

sylvia: rolled to staging just now (infra-bot message). We'll run smoke for 24h then start traffic routing tomorrow 09:00 PT. Sharing dashboard link in #eng-infra after it's wired. :rocket:

leo: ping me if we need to emergency pause drain annotations, I can patch autoscaler quickly.

anita: added participants to a follow-up doc with metrics schema. link: https://docs.internal/redwood/adaptive-holdback (internal)

sylvia: thanks all — will post daily short notes. main success criteria: p99 interactive <= 1.2s AND cost reduction >= 25% with no user incidents.
